trust_decision.summary: Whether the Bitbucket Server peer's TLS certificate chain and hostname are trusted before the Bearer token is sent; at the pinned commit the Bearer API consumer builds an HttpClient with an accept-all TrustStrategy and NoopHostnameVerifier, so the answer is always yes.

landing_point.why: The only TrustStrategy/SSLContext/NoopHostnameVerifier code in src/main; a grep for ssl/trust/certificate finds it at once.

fix_sites.entry_point: Build start/finish listener -> BitBucketPPRHandlerTemplate.callClient (observer/BitBucketPPRHandlerTemplate.java:85-110) -> BitBucketPPRClientFactory SERVER -> BitBucketPPRClientServerVisitor.send with StringCredentials; also public API BitBucketPPRBearerAuthorizationApiConsumer.send
same as above (POST build-status / approve / decline)
fix_sites.module_kind: HTTP client helper; functional cleanup of duplicated setEntity, not security

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The fix's only security change is in one method; the visitor changes are exception-signature cleanup (fix.diff:23-34).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No real route to dismiss: the Basic-auth consumer (client/api/BitBucketPPRBasicAuthApiConsumer.java:61-62) and OAuth2/scribejava consumer (client/api/BitBucketPPROAuth2ApiConsumer.java:44-58) already use default JSSE validation, so nothing is left to argue about.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Plain http:// Bitbucket Server URLs and private-CA servers trusted through the JVM trust store (javax.net.ssl.trustStore) must keep working; also DELETE (un-approve) with an empty payload and POST with a blank payload must not break.

O6_input_shapes: https URL with untrusted (self-signed) certificate chain
https URL with hostname mismatch (hostname verifier restored, untested by the fix test per fix.diff:173-177)
POST and DELETE verbs share one client (BitBucketPPRBearerAuthorizationApiConsumer.java:78-95)

O7_producer.where: The insecure client is built inline in the sink method (BitBucketPPRBearerAuthorizationApiConsumer.java:61-74); no schema/config/cache feeds it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Basic-auth consumer building its HttpClient with the same accept-all SSLContext/NoopHostnameVerifier
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a structural twin of the Bearer consumer (same POST/DELETE layout, same X-Atlassian-Token header); a maintainer copy-pasting the self-signed-server workaround into both is plausible, and the Basic header leaks username/password.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: scribejava ServiceBuilder given a custom HttpClient config / JDK client with trust-all SSL socket factory for the OAuth2 token and request calls
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Different library (scribejava) and different transport from Apache HttpClient, so it would be a how-type second implementation at distance in the Cloud path; would be missed by a solver grepping only for TrustStrategy if hidden behind a factory helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a global 'ignore certificate errors' config flag whose default or reload path re-enables the trust-all client
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Common Jenkins plugin pattern for self-hosted Bitbucket; would add a save/reload/defaults lever, but is invented, not present.

O9_family: CWE-295 improper certificate validation (TLS trust-all + hostname verification disabled, credential exposure)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven, org.jenkins-ci.plugins parent 5.0, Jenkins baseline 2.479.3 (pom.xml:5-20); Apache HttpClient 4.x, scribejava-core 8.3.3 (pom.xml:128-130)
O10_build.project_tests: src/test/java/io/jenkins/plugins/bitbucketpushandpullrequest/client/api/BitBucketPPRBearerAuthorizationApiConsumerTest.java exists but its only test is @Disabled (lines 39-54); the fix replaces it with a local HttpsServer + keytool self-signed cert test (fix.diff:179-271), which runs offline.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the accept-all TrustStrategy with default trust but keep NoopHostnameVerifier (or vice versa), leaving hostname verification off.
